overview: The Planning and Permitting Committee is a committee of the Medford City Council responsible for reviewing and drafting municipal land use regulations, zoning code overhauls, development standards, and property ordinances. Its work covers reviewing comprehensive zoning updates, corridor master plans, environmental performance standards, and housing regulations in coordination with city planning staff and external consultants. The archive covers 36 meetings of the committee held between February 28, 2024, and May 5, 2026. Over this span, the committee has systematically processed citywide zoning changes, including specialized districts for major transit corridors and commercial squares, environmental green scoring, and state-mandated accessory dwelling unit provisions. At its most recent meeting, the committee advanced a draft rezoning proposal for the Boston Avenue corridor and Tufts Institutional District for a joint session with the Community Development Board.

threads.name: Comprehensive zoning overhaul and recodification
threads.summary: In March 2024, consultants from Innes Associates presented a multi-phase framework and timeline for a comprehensive overhaul of the city's zoning code (M02#1, M04#1). The committee reviewed proposed updates to use tables, definitions, and municipal exemptions, bundling them with a digitized GIS zoning map to report out to the full City Council (M06#9, M07#1, M07#2). The body subsequently conducted mapping workshops to examine setbacks, lot sizes, and widespread parcel non-conformities across neighborhoods (M09#1, M10#1). In March 2026, the committee took up technical and procedural cleanup amendments concerning building and dwelling definitions, keeping the item in committee for structured tiering by staff (M33#1).

threads.name: Mystic Avenue corridor rezoning
threads.summary: The committee designated the Mystic Avenue commercial corridor as an urgent rezoning priority to replace auto-oriented parcels with walkable, multi-story mixed-use development (M08#5, M11#1). Consultants proposed curb setbacks, active ground floors, and height allowances tied to incentive zoning (M11#1, M13#3). The committee directed drafting under Option B to incorporate life sciences and refine sub-district dimensional standards (M13#3, M14#2). The committee voted to refer the finalized Mystic Avenue Corridor District zoning proposal to the City Council for referral to the Community Development Board (M15#1).

threads.name: Salem Street corridor rezoning
threads.summary: Rezoning for the Salem Street corridor was initiated in mid-2024 alongside Mystic Avenue to address neighborhood commercial nodes and corridor parcels (M08#5, M10#2). Committee members and planning staff debated building heights, step-backs, and parcel viability on smaller lots (M11#3, M11#4). Consultants drafted a proposal establishing mixed-use and multi-unit residential sub-districts to correct existing zoning loopholes and preserve residential blocks (M16#2, M17#1). The committee reviewed incentive-based height bonuses, parking ratios, and compatibility standards before voting to refer the Salem Street proposal to the City Council for referral to the Community Development Board (M18#1).

threads.name: Neighborhood and urban residential zoning
threads.summary: In January 2025, consultants presented a zoning proposal to replace single-family districts with tiered neighborhood residential zones allowing accessory units and historic conversions (M19#1). The committee approved motions to scale down proposed density tiers across several neighborhoods and requested improved public outreach (M19#2, M20#2). Discussions focused on establishing a density gradient, capping building heights at three stories, and protecting existing non-conforming single-family homes from unnecessary variance burdens (M21#1, M21#3). Although the committee voted to refer the draft residential proposal to the City Council in February 2025, Council President Zac Bears proposed in July 2025 to extend the review of residential districts into 2026 (M22#7, M30#1).

threads.name: Accessory Dwelling Unit regulations
threads.summary: The committee initially addressed accessory dwellings through definition updates for manufactured and tiny homes during the Phase 1 zoning review (M06#6). Following state legislative changes, the committee reviewed local regulations to govern accessory dwelling units in residential districts, exploring special permits and short-term rental bans (M21#3, M23#2, M24#2). The committee evaluated draft rules allowing ADUs while setting local special permit standards for second units on single lots and conversions of historic accessory structures (M26#3). The committee voted to refer the ADU zoning regulations favorably to the City Council for referral to the Community Development Board (M26#4).

threads.name: Commercial squares and smart growth zoning
threads.summary: In early 2025, consultants introduced a commercial zoning framework dividing commercial areas into mixed-use sub-districts, focusing on Medford Square and West Medford Square (M23#1, M24#1, M25#1). The committee refined district maps to establish daylight standards and angular planes protecting residential abutters in Medford Square and increased density near the commuter rail stop in West Medford Square (M26#1, M26#2). Both square proposals were referred favorably to the City Council for referral to the Community Development Board (M26#4). In 2026, the committee evaluated 40R Smart Growth zoning overlays to secure state reimbursements for the high school building project and directed planning staff to begin work on a 40R strategy for Medford Square (M34#4, M34#5).

threads.name: Boston Avenue and Tufts Institutional District rezoning
threads.summary: The committee began exploring institutional zoning for Tufts University and rezoning along minor corridors like Boston Avenue in mid-2025 (M27#2, M29#1, M30#2). In 2026, consultants presented data showing widespread parcel non-conformity along Boston Avenue, while planning staff outlined legal limitations under the Dover Amendment regarding campus regulation (M34#1, M34#3, M35#1, M35#6). The committee considered boundary adjustments, provisions for private student housing, and three mixed-use sub-districts with incentive height tiers (M35#3, M36#1, M36#3). The committee approved amendments prohibiting drive-throughs and gas stations and referred the draft proposal to the City Council for a joint meeting with the Community Development Board (M36#2, M36#7).

threads.name: Housing stability and property management ordinances
threads.summary: In February 2024, the committee reviewed the rollout of the Housing Stability Notification Ordinance and voted to keep the paper in committee to coordinate with the Building Department (M01#1). In December 2025, Chair Kit Collins presented a draft condominium conversion ordinance with tenant relocation payments and notification rules, which was kept in committee for further administrative consultation (M31#1). In early 2026, the committee reviewed a proposed vacant properties ordinance introducing registration requirements, online registries, and escalating fee structures (M32#1, M33#2). The committee approved a motion to refer the revised vacant building ordinance to the regular City Council meeting pending legal review and further edits (M33#2).

It also worked on climate action alignment, green score standards, short-term rental rules, and tenant protection ordinances.
